chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Six غلامs were brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام who had been in the Euphrates, and one of them drowned. Then three of them testified against two, saying that those two had drowned him, and two testified against the three, saying that the three had drowned him. So ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled that three-fifths of the diyah was upon the two, and two-fifths upon the three.

key_terms.أَخْمَاسٍ: fifths, used here for apportioning liability
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.غَرَّقَاهُ: the two caused him to drown
key_terms.غَرَّقُوهُ: the three caused him to drown

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام rule in a case where conflicting witnesses accused different groups of causing a drowning?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام in a case of disputed liability for drowning. It shows the division of diyah according to the balance of testimony and reflects the precision of legal judgment in shared criminal responsibility.
